item.title: Planet Money: Is this how the great international borrowing spree ends?
item.description:
In recent months, there have been serious whispers about an outrageous possibility: that one day soon, France — the seventh largest economy in the world — might not be able to pay back its debts. Right now, protesters in France are complaining about crumbling schools, the lack of teachers, and the overall high cost of living. But the government is struggling to find the money to address all the country’s problems.

France is in a lot of debt. It has been borrowing record amounts of money. So have many other countries including the U.S., the U.K., Italy, Canada. For more than a decade, there has been an international borrowing spree going on. Now, as interest rates climb, that borrowing spree might have to come to an end. And the consequences could get ugly.

item.title: Radiolab: The Buried Bodies Case
item.description:
In 1973, a massive manhunt in New York's Adirondack Mountains ended when police captured a man named Robert Garrow. And that’s when this story really gets started.

In this episode, that we first released in 2016, we consider a string of barbaric crimes by a hated man, and the attorney who, when called to defend him, also wound up defending a core principle of our legal system. When Frank Armani learned his client’s most gruesome secrets, he made a morally startling decision that stunned the world and goes to the heart of what it means to be a defense attorney - how far should lawyers go to provide the best defense to the worst people?

NOTE: This episode contains graphic descriptions of sexual assault and violence, listener discretion is advised.

Special thanks to Tom Alibrandi, author of Privileged Information, with Frank Armani, Laurence Gooley, author of Terror in the Adirondacks: The True Story of Serial Killer Robert F. item.title: NerdWallet's Smart Money Podcast: Should You Manage Your Own Mortgage Escrow? Plus, Decoding 2026 Election Slogans
item.description:
Learn whether managing your own mortgage escrow pays off and what popular election slogans could mean for your money.
Can you manage your own escrow account instead of letting your mortgage servicer pay your property taxes and homeowners insurance? Hosts Sean Pyles, CFP®, and Elizabeth Ayoola welcome housing Nerd Kate Wood to weigh the pros and cons of do-it-yourself escrow. They discuss how escrow fits into your monthly mortgage payment, when a lender might grant an escrow waiver, and why FHA loans and private mortgage insurance can take the choice off the table. They also run the numbers on how much interest you could earn by holding the money yourself, what happens when an escrow account comes up short, and why some mortgage hacks on social media don’t tell the full story.
What do candidates actually mean when they say “tax the rich,” “affordability” or “Medicare for All”? Senior news writer Anna Helhoski joins Sean and Elizabeth to decode the campaign slogans on mailers, ads and bumper stickers ahead of Election Day. They discuss how one slogan can cover very different taxes, how candidates are framing the cost of groceries, utilities and healthcare, and why “affordable housing” means something different from race to race.

item.title: Filmspotting: Zuck Dynasty, Pt. 2 — The Social Reckoning
item.description:
A few weeks out from The Social Reckoning’’s tepid theatrical debut, it’s safe to say Aaron Sorkin’s “spiritual sequel” to 2010’s The Social Network won’t match its successor’s box-office success, nor is it likely to be as fondly remembered in 16 years’ time. There are many ways in which the newer film goes astray, which we cover in our opening discussion of Reckoning, before bringing Network back in for Connections to consider how much of each film’s vision of Mark Zuckerberg’s social-media empire can be attributed to/blamed on Sorkin specifically. Then in a Zuck-inspired Your Next Picture Show, we briefly review a very long documentary about another tech billionaire whose name has become something of a four-letter word over the years: Alex Gibney’s Musk.

item.title: Search Engine: What it’s like when Elizabeth Holmes decides to destroy your life
item.description:

To Tyler Shultz, though, she’s still his former boss who tried to take apart his life and his family. What it was like working at Theranos, and what it’s been like watching the internet react to the new Elizabeth Holmes.
